questions.q: By default, how do multiple jobs in one workflow run relative to each other?
options: In parallel, on separate runners
Only the first job ever runs automatically
One at a time, in the order they're listed
They share a single runner and filesystem
questions.explain: GitHub runs every job in a workflow in parallel on its own runner unless something — like needs — forces an order.

questions.q: What does `needs: lint` on a job called `test` do?
options: Makes lint and test run at the exact same time
Has no effect on job order, only on step order
Renames the test job to lint
Makes test wait for lint to finish successfully before starting, and skip if lint fails
questions.explain: needs creates a dependency — the dependent job waits for the named job to succeed, and is skipped if it fails.

questions.q: What is the difference between a `uses:` step and a `run:` step?
options: uses: is for jobs, run: is for workflows
uses: executes a pre-built action; run: executes a raw shell command
There is no difference — they are interchangeable syntax
uses: only works on Windows runners; run: only works on Linux
questions.explain: uses: calls a reusable action like actions/checkout@v4, while run: executes a shell command directly on the runner.

questions.q: Why might Northbridge Retail register a self-hosted runner instead of using ubuntu-latest?
options: Because GitHub-hosted runners cannot run npm commands
To give a job direct network access to something hosted runners can't reach, like an internal staging database
Because self-hosted runners are always faster than GitHub-hosted ones
Self-hosted runners are required for every workflow
questions.explain: Self-hosted runners are machines you manage yourself, useful when a job needs access to internal infrastructure a GitHub-hosted runner can't reach.

questions.q: On a finished run's summary page, what does a red X next to a step indicate?
options: The entire repository has been deleted
That specific step failed
The job is still queued and hasn't started
The workflow file has a YAML syntax error that prevented any run
questions.explain: Each step gets its own status icon — a red X marks the exact step that failed, which is where you'd start reading the log.
